walkthroughs.body_html:
Kinetics & Equilibria — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Kinetics & Equilibria brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Kinetics & Equilibria.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Increasing temperature increases the rate mainly because:
options: More collisions occur
A greater fraction of collisions exceed E_a
Concentration increases
Activation energy falls

mcqs.q: If [A] doubles and the rate quadruples, the order with respect to A is:
How does the rate of an SN2 reaction depend on concentrations?
options: A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
SN2 reactions are first order overall because only the substrate matters.
SN2 reactions are zero order because they happen in one step.
Rate is first order in both substrate AND nucleophile (overall second order) because both are involved in the rate-determining step.

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: SN2 reactions are zero order because they happen in one step.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

mcqs.q: Why does increasing temperature increase the rate of reaction significantly?
options: SN2 reactions are zero order because they happen in one step.
Higher temperature increases the concentration of the reactants.
Mainly because a much larger fraction of collisions have energy at least equal to the activation energy; collision frequency increases only slightly.
Particles collide much more frequently at higher temperature, which is the main reason for the rate increase.
